title: Finite-coefficient exceptional adjunction and coefficient mates over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of positive characteristic $p$, let $\ell\ne p$ be prime, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\geq1$. For a finite coefficient ring $A$ occurring below, let $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ mean the full triangulated subcategory of the ordinary derived category $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ of $A_T$-module sheaves with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, admitting etale-origin witnesses on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Choose a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and put $F_A=Rg_{*,A}j_!$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. For $T=X,Y$, let $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ be the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $f_A^\times$ be the ordinary etale right adjoint of $Rg_{\mathrm{et},*,A}j_{\mathrm{et},!}$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], with its unit and counit. On the etale-origin finite constructible subcategory define
$$G_A=Rf_A^!=\nu_X^* f_A^\times R\nu_{Y,*}.$$
The adjunction on this subcategory is transported using the site-comparison unit and the compact-support comparison [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison, lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. This construction is made for the arbitrary field $k$ just specified.

The functors $F_A,G_A$ preserve these finite-Tor constructible categories and $F_A\dashv G_A$ there, with the geometric finite-coefficient units $\eta_A$ and counits $\epsilon_A$. Consider either a quotient $A_m\to A_n$, $m\ge n$, or the finite-free map $R/t^n\to S/t^nS$ for a finite extension $E\subset F$ with valuation ring $S=\mathcal O_F$. Put $T_X=-\otimes_A^L B_X$ and $T_Y=-\otimes_A^L B_Y$ for the corresponding coefficient extensions. The canonical projection comparison
$$q_{A,B}:T_YF_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_X$$
is a natural isomorphism of ordinary derived functors on $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$. Its right-adjoint mate
$$b_{A,B}:T_XG_A\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BT_Y$$
is a natural isomorphism on $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Specifically, $b_{A,B}$ is the $F_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $T_Y\epsilon_A\circ q_{A,B,G_A}^{-1}$; consequently
$$\epsilon_B\circ F_B(b_{A,B})=T_Y\epsilon_A\circ q_{A,B,G_A}^{-1}.$$
For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ the unit identity is
$$G_B(q_{A,B,K})\circ b_{A,B,F_AK}\circ T_X(\eta_{A,K})=\eta_{B,T_XK}.$$ All functors and natural transformations here are in ordinary derived categories. Under the canonical tensor reassociation for $A\to B\to C$, the projection maps satisfy $q_{A,C}=q_{B,C}\circ T_{B,C}(q_{A,B})$ (with the necessary whiskerings), and the mates satisfy $b_{A,C}=b_{B,C}\circ T_{B,C}(b_{A,B})$. Identity coefficient maps give identity comparisons. These are equalities of natural transformations, also compatible with the canonical compactification-refinement isomorphisms. The same equalities hold in mixed diagrams of the displayed quotient and finite-free coefficient maps. Thus extension from $R$ to $S$ compares the whole exceptional coefficient system, including its counit, on the cofinal quotients $S/t^nS$; these are the subsequence $S/v^{en}$ for a uniformizer $v$ of $S$ and ramification index $e$. No integral inverse-limit adjunction, rational or condensed comparison is asserted.

source.place: Finite-stage counit-normalized coefficient comparison, extended from its smooth chart case to arbitrary separated finite-type k-morphisms by closed-support triangles and local affine embeddings; enhanced and finite-free system clauses are agent-written supplements.

proof.text: Work first on ordinary etale sites. All schemes in a compactification are finite type over k and hence Noetherian: apply finite-type-over-Noetherian to Spec(k), whose only ideals are 0 and k. The coefficient rings A_n are finite local rings by the DVR and finite-quotient statements. For E contained in F, uniqueness of the extending absolute value identifies the restriction from F with the absolute value on E, so R is a subring of S and |t|_F<1. The DVR expansion in S writes t=u v^e with u a unit and e>=1; hence t^nS=v^{en}S, and S/tS is finite by the finite-quotient statement. Here is the missing finite-generation argument, rather than an invocation of a geometric coefficient lemma. Choose representatives b_1,...,b_h in S for all elements of S/tS. Starting with x_0=x in S, recursively choose i_r with x_r=b_{i_r}+t x_{r+1}. Then x=sum_{r<N}t^r b_{i_r}+t^N x_N, and |t^N x_N|_F<=|t|_F^N tends to zero. For each i, the partial coefficient sums sum_{r<N,i_r=i}t^r are Cauchy in E; completeness gives a limit a_i in the closed unit ball R. Taking limits in the finite sum gives x=sum_i a_i b_i. Thus S is finitely generated over R, and it is torsion-free since R and S lie in fields. The DVR finite-free lemma makes S finite free over R; reducing a finite basis gives B=S/t^nS finite free over A=R/t^n. The ideal identity above is independent of the units relating uniformizers. Thus every ring in the question is a positive DVR quotient, is finite Noetherian, and is annihilated by an ell-power invertible on every scheme here: apply the same positive-valuation expansion to ell in each valuation ring. Choose intervals with a<=b, enlarging an interval if necessary for a zero object.

proof.text: For any k-map h between finite-type k-schemes, lem-kun-0f10(1), interpreted by def-kun-cd, supplies a finite c with R^q h_* M=0 for q>c for all torsion abelian sheaves. The restriction-of-scalars comparison, applied to Z \to A, transfers this bound to A-module sheaves; the forgetful functor is exact and detects zero objects. In particular this applies to the proper map g and to every complementary open j used below. No assumption on the absolute cohomological dimension of k is made. For bounded inputs, the bound implies Rh_* sends cohomological [a,b] into [a,b+c]: filter by the finitely many cohomology truncations, use Rh_*(M[-r])=Rh_*M[-r], and the long exact cohomology sequences of those triangles.

proof.text: Rh_* preserves ordinary bounded constructible finite-Tor complexes for these h and DVR stages A. Indeed thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility gives bounded constructibility. If K has Tor amplitude [a,b], use lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible to represent K by flat constructible terms in [a,b]. Tensoring those terms with any finite A-algebra B gives flat constructible B-module sheaves in the same degrees: on a common finite constructible stratification their fibres are finite modules, and B-flatness follows from (P tensor_A B) tensor_B N=P tensor_A N. In particular K tensor_A^L kappa is bounded constructible in [a,b]. Since kappa is a finitely presented A-module and K belongs to D^-, lem-sf-projection-finite-constant and Step 2 identify (Rh_*K) tensor_A^L kappa with Rh_*(K tensor_A^L kappa). Its cohomology vanishes outside [a,b+c]. Apply lem-exc-residue-tor-test on the target to obtain Tor amplitude [a,b+c]. The same argument with M=B in the projection lemma gives the canonical coefficient comparison T Rh_* K \to Rh_* T K as an isomorphism after restriction of B-scalars. The restriction-of-scalars comparison identifies the target with the B-linear direct image; restriction detects isomorphisms, so this is the B-linear projection isomorphism itself, for both coefficient maps in the question.

proof.text: For an open immersion j, exact extension by zero preserves bounded constructibility: extend a constructibility stratification on its open domain by the closed complement, on which the sheaf is zero. Its stalks are the original stalks or zero. Consequently extension by zero takes a flat constructible model to a flat constructible model of the same length, and the natural map T j_! \to j_! T is an isomorphism: use a flat model and check its termwise tensor map on stalks. Conservativity of geometric stalks proves isomorphism of this specified map. Composing with Step 3 for g proves that F_A^et=Rg_*j_! preserves D^b_ctf and that its canonical projection comparison q is invertible. This is the projection comparison built by the geometric open/proper operations, not a newly chosen isomorphism.

proof.text: The ambient etale adjoint f_A^times exists by thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint. Use the unbounded compactification and composition comparisons of lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons; every map here is separated of finite type between Noetherian schemes. For the local factors and their composites, thm-nagata-compactification gives compactifiability: the targets are quasi-compact and quasi-separated (they are separated finite-type k-schemes). Transposing its left-functor composition isomorphism by the two ambient adjunctions identifies (gf)^times with f^times g^times on the whole ordinary derived categories, with the composite unit and counit. Thus this use of composition does not presuppose that an exceptional image is bounded below. Source-open locality is precisely the canonical isomorphism of lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality. For an open target restriction v, v_! dashv v^* and the same composition comparison give the corresponding v^* factor in the right adjoint. All these identifications use conjugate adjunctions and the mate-pasting identities, so their units and counits have fixed normalizations.

proof.text: For a closed immersion i:Z\toP between finite-type k-schemes, its complementary open j is quasi-compact since P is Noetherian. Step 2 gives the uniform vanishing required by prop-exc-closed-tor. Theorem thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility, applied to j and a constructible sheaf in degree zero, gives constructibility of each R^qj_* of that sheaf. Thus every hypothesis of prop-exc-closed-tor holds, and i^times=Ri^! preserves D^b_ctf. For a projection pi:A^r_V\toV, thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity identifies pi^times L with pi^*L(r)[2r] by the adjoint of the stated trace. Exact inverse image preserves constructibility and flatness; the twist is locally constant and etale locally free of rank one by lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback, applied to m=ell^s annihilating A (m is invertible on these k-schemes). Hence this expression preserves D^b_ctf. Cover Y by finitely many affine V and each inverse image by finitely many affine U. Finite algebra generators give a closed immersion U\toA^r_V factoring f|U. By Step 5 and open adjunctions, u^* f^times L identifies with i^times pi^times v^*L, where u:U\toX and v:V\toY. The right side is bounded constructible finite-Tor. These properties glue across the finite open cover: take the minimum of the finitely many lower bounds and maximum of upper bounds, and glue the finite constructibility stratifications. Consequently f^times preserves D^b_ctf over the original arbitrary k.

proof.text: For any finite coefficient ring here, etale/pro-etale comparison identifies bounded etale constructible complexes with intrinsically constructible bounded pro-etale complexes. It also identifies their finite-Tor subcategories. In the forward direction, pull back a bounded flat constructible etale model: exactness of nu^* and the flat-term pullback assertion for ringed topoi give a bounded flat model on the pro-etale site. In the reverse direction, write K=nu^*K0 by constructible derived origin; if K has Tor amplitude [a,b], its tensor with the constant residue field has cohomology in [a,b]. Tensor-pullback compatibility identifies this with nu^*(K0 tensor_A^L kappa). Exactness and full faithfulness of nu^* on D^+ reflect this interval, so the residue-field Tor test shows that K0 has the same Tor amplitude. The etale origin is bounded, so all these uses of D^+ full faithfulness are legitimate. Apply compact-support site comparison to identify F_A nu_X^* with nu_Y^* F_A^et. It follows from Steps 4 and 6 that F_A and G_A=nu_X^* f_A^times Rnu_{Y,*} preserve the stated pro-etale category. For K=nu_X^*K0 and L=nu_Y^*L0 the Hom chain Hom(F_A K,L)=Hom(F_A^et K0,L0)=Hom(K0,f_A^times L0)=Hom(K,G_A L) gives the required adjunction. Each equality uses the specified comparison and unit, so its unit and counit are precisely the transported geometric ones. Tensor-pullback compatibility transports the specified q of Step 4 as well.

proof.text: For the smooth affine-space projection $\pi:\mathbf A^r_V\to V$, apply det-sp-reduction-exceptional to $A\to B$. Step 1 verifies its finite commutative $\ell$-primary hypotheses for both coefficient maps. It gives an invertible pro-etale coefficient mate characterized by the displayed counit-transpose equation, with chart value the tensor reassociation of $\pi^*(-)(r)[2r]$. Use the same standard compactification for both functors. The site/coefficient square and the counit-transport clause of lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility identify the ordinary-etale projection map of Step 4, after site transport, with the named pro-etale coefficient map in that equation. Its hypotheses hold by Steps 1, 4 and 7: the schemes are separated finite type over $k$, and the inputs and exceptional outputs are bounded constructible finite-Tor. By det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer the transported counit is $\nu_V^*(\epsilon_A^{\mathrm{et}})\circ c_{\pi,A}^{-1}$, exactly the counit used in Step 7. Apply det-sp-unique-right-adjoint to identify its right adjoint with the one used in det-sp-reduction-exceptional, preserving this counit. Under these identifications the invertible mate satisfies $\epsilon_B F_B(b_\pi)=T\epsilon_A q_\pi^{-1}$; uniqueness of the adjunction transpose makes it our specified $b_\pi$. The cited site/coefficient square carries this equation back to the ordinary-etale equation. Full faithfulness of the site equivalences of Step 7 reflects invertibility, giving the ordinary-etale projection case needed in Step 12. For $r=0$ these are the identity adjunction and tensor reassociation.

source.place: Charts and uniqueness of transposes; the site/coefficient square is the separately cited lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility, and the transported counit is det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer.

proof.text: For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow P$ with open complement $j$, construct support triangles on ordinary complexes. For a module sheaf $M$ put $H(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$. The kernel is supported on $Z$; the fully faithful supported-sheaf equivalence of lem-kun-04ca, transported to modules by naturality for scalar multiplications, identifies it with $i_*H(M)$. Every map $i_*N\to M$ factors uniquely through this kernel: its composite to $j_*j^*M$ is zero under $j^*\dashv j_*$ because $j^*i_*N=0$. Hence $i_*\dashv H$, with counit the kernel inclusion. Choose functorial degreewise-injective K-injective representatives $I$ using the Grothendieck and replacement lemmas. On every etale $V\to P$, $V\times_P U\to V$ is monic; injective restriction along monomorphisms gives surjectivity of $I^r(V)\to I^r(V\times_PU)$. Thus $0\to i_*H(I)\to I\to j_*j^*I\to0$ is a natural short exact sequence of complexes. Open restriction preserves K-injectives by the localization lemma, so the last term represents $Rj_*j^*L$. The closed stalk formula, zero stalks off $Z$, and exact conservative stalks show $i_*$ is exact, also on modules since exactness is detected after forgetting scalars. Exactness of $i_*$ and the termwise adjunction show $H(I)$ represents $Ri^!L$: $H$ preserves K-injectives, and the Hom-into-K-injective bijections derive $i_*\dashv H$ with this counit. Apply the short-exact-sequence triangle lemma. This realizes precisely the counit/unit support triangle of lem-exc-closed-support-triangle, with a natural connecting map.

proof.text: To compare support triangles for $A\to B$, it is enough to check the specified $B$-linear mate after exact restriction of scalars. Choose a K-flat resolution $Q\to B_P$ with flat terms over $A_P$ and use the representative $I$ of Step 9. Tensor its short exact support sequence with $Q$. This remains degreewise exact: each tensor by $Q^r$ is exact and the sums in total tensor are exact (direct sums are filtered colimits of finite sums in the Grothendieck module category). Put $N=\operatorname{Tot}(Q\otimes_A I)$ and choose its functorial degreewise-injective K-injective replacement $a:N\to J$ over $A_P$. The chain maps $a$ and $Q\otimes j_*j^*I\to j_*(j^*Q\otimes j^*I)\xrightarrow{j_*j^*a}j_*j^*J$ commute strictly with the restriction units, by the sectionwise tensor map and naturality. They induce a unique map of kernels $Q\otimes i_*H(I)\to i_*H(J)$, hence a map of short exact sequences. The triangle lemma makes it a morphism of distinguished triangles, including the connecting arrow. In the ordinary $A$-derived category its middle map represents the identity of $\operatorname{Res}(TL)$. Its right map is the canonical projection comparison of Step 3, identified with $\operatorname{Res}(Rj_{*,B}j^*TL)$ by the restriction-of-scalars comparison. It is invertible. The left map is therefore invertible by triangle two-out-of-three. This construction uses an $A$-flat model of $B$ only after restriction; it asserts no strict $B$-action on its flat terms.

source.place: Tag 09XP support sequence; tensor via Stacks 06YS (sites-cohomology-lemma-K-flat-resolution); naturality of the ordinary short-exact-sequence triangle.

proof.text: Identify the left map with the specified mate, rather than an arbitrary triangle completion. The $B$-coefficient support triangle, after restriction to $A$, has middle term $\operatorname{Res}(TL)$ and right term $Rj_{*,A}j^*\operatorname{Res}(TL)$ with its unit, by the restriction comparison. Its left term and $i_*H(J)$ are supported on $Z$. For any supported derived object $W=i_*M$, the open adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(W,Rj_*D[r])=\operatorname{Hom}(j^*W,D[r])=0$ for every $r$. Here $j^*i_*M=0$ follows termwise from the support equivalence and exactness of inverse image. The exact Hom sequence of a triangle therefore makes maps from $W$ to either left term bijective with maps from $W$ to the middle term. Applying this bijection twice gives the unique counit-compatible identification of the two left terms. The source left term of Step 10 is supported too and identifies with $i_*\operatorname{Res}(T Ri_A^!L)$ via the closed-immersion projection isomorphism of Step 3. Under these identifications its map to the middle term is $T\epsilon_{i,A}$. The definition of $b_i$ says that $i_*\operatorname{Res}(b_i)$ has precisely this same composite. Uniqueness in the Hom bijection identifies the maps, so $i_*\operatorname{Res}(b_i)$ is invertible. Since $i^*i_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$, $i_*$ detects isomorphisms; exact restriction of scalars detects them as well. Thus the specified $B$-linear $b_i$ is invertible. In particular neither injectivity of a restricted $B$-injective nor flatness of $B/A$ was assumed.

source.place: Tag 09XP support triangle; ordinary Hom exactness (Stacks 0149) identifies its supported term and fixes the coefficient mate by its counit.

proof.text: The compactification-refinement and composition equations for the specified projection maps are exactly the last clauses of lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility; Steps 1, 4 and 7 verify its finite-ring and bounded constructible finite-Tor hypotheses. Applying mate-pasting now identifies the coefficient mate for a composite with the pasted mates of its factors and identifies its restriction on each affine U of Step 6 with the composite of b_i, b_pi, and the coefficient identity for v^*. The last identity follows directly from exact pullback commuting with coefficient tensor. Source locality identifies this restriction with u^*b_f, with the adjunctions transported as in Step 5. Steps 8 and 11 make it invertible on each U. Its cone has zero cohomology on an open cover, hence zero geometric stalks; geometric-stalk conservativity applied to the cohomology sheaves proves b_f invertible. Via Step 7 this proves invertibility of the exact b_{A,B} in the question for quotient maps. The same argument proves it for the finite-free map because Step 3, the smooth coefficient-mate comparison of Step 8 and the support triangle also apply to that map. Alternatively for the finite-free map choose an A-basis of B: both T and q identify with the same finite direct sum, and the right-adjoint mate is that finite-sum identification by counit naturality. This alternative is only a check; the defined b is basis-independent.

proof.text: The counit identity is the defining equation for the transpose b, so holds as an equality of the specified maps. For the unit equation, let alpha=G_B(q_K) b_{F_A K} T_X(eta_{A,K}). Its F_B dashv G_B transpose is epsilon_{B,F_BT_XK} F_B(alpha). Counit naturality moves q_K to the outside, and the defining counit equation for b changes this expression to q_K (T_Y epsilon_{A,F_AK}) q^{-1}_{G_AF_AK} F_BT_X(eta_{A,K}). Naturality of q changes the last two factors to T_YF_A(eta_{A,K}) q_K^{-1}. The A-triangle identity now reduces the whole composite to q_K id q_K^{-1}=id. The transpose of id is eta_{B,T_XK}, proving exactly the displayed unit equation. This is elementary adjunction algebra, using no invertibility principle for mates.

proof.text: It remains to check ordinary coefficient-system equalities. The canonical derived-tensor associators and unitors, with their naturality and associativity diagrams, are clause (4) of det-sp-scalar-extension-functor on the ordinary pro-etale categories; its finite commutative primary-ring hypotheses hold by Step 1. They are computed by K-flat representatives as in clause (1). For $A\to B\to C$, transpose the two projection composites under the derived inverse/direct-image adjunction. Both become the same iterated evaluation $h^*Rh_*K\to K$, extended to $C$, since the composite counit is the product of the two counits. The same argument for open extension is termwise extension by zero and summandwise tensor. Thus the projection composites agree, including identity coefficient maps. Step 12 gives compatibility with compactification refinements and geometric compositions. The mate-pasting lemma now gives the stated equalities for $b$: transpose the two candidate composites under $F_C\dashv G_C$; both give $T_{A,C}\epsilon_A\circ q_{A,C}^{-1}$, so they coincide. The unit identity of Step 13 and the defining counit identity are preserved under these equalities. Any mixed diagram of the permitted quotient and finite-free maps is checked by the same transposition and tensor reassociation, independently of bases. This concerns finite systems of ordinary functors and natural transformations only. The right adjoints are already constructed in Steps 5–7; no right adjoint on a category of towers or lifting of a family of derived maps is required.

source.place: Ordinary derived coefficient composition: Stacks 06YS and 06YU; current blueprint sk-prop-sp-unique-adjoint/sk-prop-sp-unique-adjoint-coefficients and finite-ring counit-transposition argument.

proof.text: Finally Step 1 writes t=u v^e with u in S^times and e>=1, so t^nS=v^{en}S and S/t^nS=S/v^{en}S as quotient rings; the cited DVR and finite-quotient statements make these precisely the finite local coefficient stages. The finite-free lemma applies using the finite-generation and torsion-free hypotheses proved explicitly in Step 1, and reducing its basis gives the finite-free extensions at each level. Given any positive integer r, choose n>=r; then en>=r. Thus the indices en form a cofinal subsystem, and all coefficient, unit and counit comparisons just proved restrict to it. This is only an assertion about finite coefficient systems; no passage to inverse limits or extension to rational or condensed coefficient categories has occurred.
